Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RetailOps: replacement quote & packaging questions

Hi Mateo,

Quick intro — I'm Samantha, Sr. Product Ops at RetailOps. We're evaluating a vendor replacement for inference serving across our personalization stack. Our procurement timeline is Q4 and we've collected a competing commercial offer that's significantly cheaper on list.

I'm attaching our RFP (RetailOps_RFP_v2.pdf) and the competitor's quote (they asked me to share). High-level:
- Current provider: EdgeServe (running on 8 GPUs, seat+consumption).
- Comp vendor (CompVendor) is offering a 12-month committed plan at 25% lower unit cost and a modest onboarding credit.

We like Redwood's runtime performance, but we need clarity on packaging (seat vs consumption), egress/pricing floors, and an honest view on migration overhead. Can we get a written response on whether you can match the unit economics or propose an alternative packaging that lands us within 10% of CompVendor?

Prefer a 30-min call early next week to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Samantha Park
Sr. Product Ops | RetailOps
T: +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: RetailOps_RFP_v2.pdf

Hi Samantha — thanks for the context and for sharing the RFP. Mateo here (Solutions/Strategic Sales) — looping in Lauren (AM) and Connor (Solutions ENG) so we can converge on the ask.

Short answers up front: we can land a competitive package in many cases, but the best outcome depends on three knobs: committed term, onboarding credit, and whether you choose seat-based or consumption billing. A few quick clarifying Qs before we model a counter:
1) What is your current monthly token/embedding volume (approx)?
2) Any hard constraints on egress or data residency?
3) Are you able to commit to a 12-month minimum or prefer a 6-month trial?

Proposed next steps: 30-min call Monday 11/17 10:00-10:30 PT — I can bring a preliminary term sheet and Connor can speak to operational lift. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Cc: Lauren — could you flag pricing/discount bands to reference (we'll keep initial asks internal)? Connor — can you prepare a rough migration effort estimate for the RFP scope (prefix caching, model compat, infra handoff)?

Best,

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: RetailOps counter strategy (draft)

Team — after reviewing the RFP and CompVendor workbook, here are mech proposals we can take into Monday's call. Please keep this thread internal.

TL;DR: We can get within ~8-10% of CompVendor's landed economics with a blended package and focused migration support. Proposed optional constructs:

Option A — Consumption-heavy (short-term win)\- 12-month committed consumption with a 15% unit discount and 2-month consumption credit applied in first 90 days.\- Migration stipend: $60k fixed credit to cover integration effort; apply as one-time invoice credit.\- Operational support: 2-week dedicated migration window with Connor as lead (reduced go-live risk).

Option B — Seat + Consumption (better retention economics)\- 12-month term with a 4-seat minimum for dedicated runtime + consumption at 18% discounted rate.\- Onboarding credit: $80k covering professional services (handshake + runbook).

Commercial guardrails: do not drop below 18% effective unit discount on any BAU consumption unless we secure a higher committed volume or multi-year deal. For procurement asks for parity pricing we can offer a one-time migration credit in lieu of permanent list price movement.

Lauren — can you quantify the revenue impact of each option (ARR slope and net new dollars) and set recommended approval thresholds? Kimberly — please check legal on whether a one-time stipend should be a credit against invoices or a separate service SOW. Connor — prepare a short migration timeline (days of effort + key checkpoints).

Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed term sheet — RetailOps replacement package (summary)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the conversation this morning. Below is a concise summary of the commercial we can offer to land close to CompVendor while preserving Redwood's economics. If this looks reasonable, we'll draft a short-term sheet and loop in legal.

Proposed commercial (high level):
- Term: 12 months committed (starts on go-live).
- Pricing: Consumption billing with a blended 18% discount off list for all token generation/embedding usage.
- Onboarding credit: $75,000 one-time invoice credit applied within 30 days of go-live.
- Migration support: Dedicated migration lead (Connor) + 4 weeks of implementation assistance (conducted as part of onboarding).
- SLA: 99.6% uptime SLA (standard Enterprise SLA language) + 24/7 escalation path during migration window.
- Optional seat bundle: If you opt for dedicated seat pool (min 4 seats), an additional 3% discount on consumption applies (bringing total to ~21% off list).

Estimated landed economics vs CompVendor: assuming your stated volume (~9M tokens/month) the blended Option above lands within ~7% of CompVendor's quoted landed cost when migration credits are amortized over 12 months. 

Next steps:
1) If accepted in principle, we will produce a formal term sheet + commercial appendix for procurement.
2) Schedule kickoff: propose Wed 11/19 10:00 PT for legal + technical scoping.

Happy to tweak if procurement pushes on a specific line item; want to make sure we don't set a precedent of permanent list discount beyond these constructs.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
